biography.plain_text: Robert E. Lorton is an American newspaper publisher whose family owned the Tulsa World for generations. Based in Tulsa, he led World Publishing and consolidated its ownership, reacquiring shares previously held outside the family. During his tenure, the company bought its rival's printing interest, before the newspaper's sale to Berkshire Hathaway.

long_biography.plain_text:
Tulsa World publisher Robert Lorton combined a journalism education with experience as a reporter before taking charge of the family newspaper. He graduated from the University of Tulsa and served in the Marine Corps Reserve. His connection to the university reached back to childhood, when he attended the groundbreaking for Lorton Hall, funded by his grandparents.

With his wife, Roxana, Lorton co-chaired two major university fundraising campaigns, supporting scholarships, faculty posts and campus development. The couple also made the lead gift for the Lorton Performance Center, completed in 2011. Roxana's father, Béla Rózsa, had taught music at the university, giving the project a particular family connection. The centre brought music and film teaching together with rehearsal rooms, studios and a concert hall.

Reducing the long to the short loses both formation and a substantive public commitment.
